Application Materials.content:
When you apply you’ll need to submit a personal statement explaining why you want to take the course. You’ll need to include information about:
- your knowledge of the subject area
- why you want to study a postgraduate qualification in this course
- how you intend to use your qualification
References are not required for this programme. Please include the required paperwork showing your first degree and your IELTS English language test score (if you are a non-native English speaker) with your application. Without these, your application may be delayed.

Application Deadlines.content:
Marketing Analytics (MSc) starts **September 2026**.
For international students, the deadline to apply for this course is **Wednesday 19 August 2026, midday UK time**. Applications may close before the expected deadline if places are filled.

Academic Requirements.content:
Typical offer: **2:1 degree**.
You’ll need a **2:1 degree** which shows evidence of quantitative or qualitative study, such as:
- Marketing
- Analytics
- Engineering
- Social Sciences
- Economics
- Management
- Statistics
- Operations Research
- Management Science
- Information Systems
- Pure Science
- Computer Science
MSc Marketing Analytics is aimed at those who have:
- an undergraduate degree in marketing and a good understanding of quantitative studies; or
- marketing work experience looking to specialise within an analytics role.
The course does not accept the following subjects:
- Language Studies – degrees that focus on learning a language or how to translate, such as 'Business English', 'Applied English', or 'Translation', are not acceptable. However, this restriction does not apply to ‘English’ and ‘English literature’ degrees of the kind taught in the UK.
- Art/Design/Vocational Studies – degrees that focus on learning a particular form of art, craft or vocation. These include degrees in art, graphic design, photography, television broadcasting, script writing, or performance/dance.
If you don't have the exact entry requirements, but you have significant work or voluntary experience in this sector, the university will assess your relevant professional experience, your subject knowledge and your aptitude for learning.
For applicants from China: Southampton accepts bachelor's degrees (学士学位) from China. To apply, applicants usually need the equivalent of a **2:1 or a 2:2 undergraduate degree** from a highly ranked Chinese university, with a minimum average grade of between **70% and 83%**, depending on the university where they studied; applicants should see the course page for exact requirements. For this course’s **2:1** requirement, Chinese equivalent entry grades are:
| Tier | GPA out of 4.0 | GPA out of 5.0 | Percentage (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier A | **2.8** | **3.5** | **70%** |
| Tier B | **3.1** | **3.88** | **75%** |
| Tier C | **3.25** | **4.06** | **80%** |
| Tier D | **3.7** | **4.63** | **88%** |
If a Chinese institution isn't listed, use the grades for **tier D**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
If English is not your first language, you must show that you can use English to the level required. [Visit the English language pages](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/studentadmin/admissions/admissions-policies/language.page) to find out which qualifications are accepted and how you can meet the requirements.
If taking IELTS, you must get at least:
| IELTS score requirement | Minimum score |
| --- | --- |
| Overall | **6.5** |
| Reading | **6.0** |
| Writing | **6.0** |
| Speaking | **6.0** |
| Listening | **6.0** |
If you do not meet the English language requirements through a test or qualification, you may be able to meet them by completing one of the [pre-sessional English programmes](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/study/pre-sessional) before you start your course.
When applying, include the required paperwork showing your IELTS English language test score if you are a non-native English speaker; without this, your application may be delayed.

Program Overview.content:
**Marketing Analytics (MSc)** is a **Master of Science** course starting **September 2026** for **1 year**. It is a **full-time** course based at **Highfield** and awarded by the **University of Southampton**.
With the marketing analytics MSc, students learn industry-specific skills to make strategic marketing decisions using data and evidence, using a multi-channel approach to analyse and interpret data. The course is for those curious about how data informs everyday marketing techniques and who want to become a marketing analyst. It incorporates industry-specific topics covered by only a small number of marketing analytics courses in the UK, including social media data analysis and text mining.
MSc Marketing Analytics is aimed at those who have an undergraduate degree in marketing and a good understanding of quantitative studies, or marketing work experience and want to specialise within an analytics role. Southampton states that it was the first university in the UK to offer a marketing analytics master's. The programme collaborates with leading industry practitioners who inform the curriculum using best-practice marketing techniques and the latest research.
Students learn how to integrate and use marketing channels within different markets or sectors; interpret and manage large datasets to make evidence-based decisions; use online analytics to analyse how consumer choices are influenced by social media; incorporate different marketing frameworks and behaviour models to create an analytical tool; use industry-standard data analysis software; and learn from traditional churn modelling models to offer customer incentives to enhance business profitability.
The course is a 12-month programme: students complete all taught modules in the first 9 months, and in the final 3 months work on a dissertation. Compulsory modules provide a balanced grounding in marketing analytics skills, and optional modules offer opportunities for specialism in areas including project management, data protection law and forecasting. The first semester builds knowledge of digital marketing analytics, including marketing in the 21st century, customer insight, data analytics, text mining and social network analytics.
The programme is accredited by [The Institute of Data and Marketing (IDM)](https://www.theidm.com/). Marketing students on an IDM-accredited course are eligible to sit a 2-hour online exam to achieve the IDM Certificate in Digital and Data-Driven Marketing. IDM Tutor for this programme: [Dr Monica Mihalache](mailto:monica.mihalache@soton.ac.uk).
The course leader is [Dr Carmen-Monica Mihalache](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/people/5xhy9y/doctor-monica-mihalache) MS, PhD, FHEA. Monica has over 12 years of experience in digital and offline communications, with focus on visual and video communication. She studied for a Master Degree in Marketing Research at Texas A&M University, worked as a Specialist Referent in Marketing for the Public National Romanian Television, and is a member of CIRCOM Network of trainers in television.
Students learn through lectures, group work, computer lab sessions, real-world case studies and data. They prepare a dissertation in a domain of interest in Marketing Analytics, use industry-standard tools for managing, analysing and presenting big data, and industry speakers from the marketing analytics field are invited to discuss current sector issues. Previous speakers have come from companies such as Alitex, LV=, and Firebrand Training. The relatively small intake means students get individual attention from module leaders.
Graduates commonly work in specialist marketing, advertising and PR agencies, and marketing departments in all sectors. Example job titles of Southampton MSc Marketing Analytics graduates include Data analyst, Marketing specialist, Research executive, Digital marketing planner, Insight analyst, Marketing analyst, Marketing assistant, Operations analyst, Performance strategist and Product manager.
Job prospects for MSc Marketing Analytics graduates: **£33k Average professional salary**, **81% In a skilled profession or further study**, and **95% Graduate employment rate**. Source: Example graduate job titles and job prospect statistics taken from The Graduate Outcomes Survey, which gathers information about graduates 15 months after finishing their course.

Curriculum.content:
Marketing Analytics (MSc) is a **1 year**, **full-time** course based at **Highfield**. The course starts in **September 2026**.
This is a **12-month course**: you’ll complete all your taught modules in the first **9 months** and in the final **3 months** you’ll work on your dissertation. Compulsory modules provide a balanced grounding in the skills of marketing analytics. You'll then choose from optional modules that provide opportunities for specialism in areas including:
- project management
- data protection law
- forecasting
The first semester will build upon your knowledge of digital marketing analytics. You'll look at marketing in the 21st century, building customer insight, data analytics and text mining and social network analytics.
For entry in academic year **2026 to 2027**, Year 1 modules:
You **must study** the following modules:
- [**Digital Marketing Strategy**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6573)
- [**Digital and Media Analytics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6528)
- [**Integrated Marketing Communication Design**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6540)
- [**Marketing Analytics & Visualizations**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6524)
- [**Research Methods for Marketing**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6572)
You **must also choose from** the following modules:
- [**Building Customer Insight**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6267)
- [**Contemporary Marketing Practice: Ethics, Innovation, and Social Responsibility**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6262)
- [**Dissertation for Marketing**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6544) — the dissertation stage involves an extended, independent investigation of a topic of your own choosing and the preparation of a **15,000 word dissertation**.
- [**International Corporate Social Responsibility and Ethics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6535)
- [**Marketing Data Science**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6260)
- [**Marketing Practice-based Project**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6518)
- [**Measuring Marketing Effectiveness**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6533)
- [**Python for Business and Marketing**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6182)
You’ll learn through a range of teaching methods, including lectures, group work, computer lab sessions, real-world case studies and data. You will prepare a dissertation in a domain of interest in Marketing Analytics. You’ll need to use the methods, techniques and skills you learn in the taught part of the programme to write a **15,000-word dissertation**. Researching and writing your dissertation will require around **600 hours**.

Financial Aid.content:
Southampton Business School (MSc) Dean Scholarship (International): Scholarships of £9,000 and £5,000 are available to international students studying an eligible postgraduate master’s at the University of Southampton Business School, including [MSc Marketing Analytics](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/marketing-analytics-masters-msc "MSc Marketing Analytics 8536 (1 year)"). If you have a 1st or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies you will get £9,000. If you have a 2:1 or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies you will get £5,000.
To get this scholarship you must:
- be an international student required to pay the oversees fees
- have a conditional or unconditional offer to study an eligible course
- achieve a 1st or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies to receive a £9,000 award
- achieve a 2:1 or an equivalent qualification in your undergraduate studies to receive a £5,000 award
Students coming from China must have studied at a [Tier A](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/international/entry-qualification-equivalencies/china/postgraduate-taught-tier-list "Chinese awarding institutions listed by tier") university. There are a further 100 awards of either £9,000 or £5,000, depending on applicant eligibility, for applicants coming from a [Tier B](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/international/entry-qualification-equivalencies/china/postgraduate-taught-tier-list "Chinese awarding institutions listed by tier") Chinese university. These scholarships will be issued on a first past the post basis with an additional eligibility requirement being that the applicants in this category pay their tuition fee deposit by **15th January 2026**.
You do not need to apply to this scholarship. If you meet the eligibility criteria, we will award you this scholarship and let you know by email.

Multiple Applications.content: If you would like to apply for both taught and research programmes, please complete a separate form for each application. If you want to apply for two taught programmes within the same Academic School please list these in order of preference as Choice 1 and Choice 2. If you want to apply for a taught programme in another School or any research programme, please fill in a separate form.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Applicants in possession of an unconditional offer of a place may request that it be deferred to the next intake. The University does not typically permit more than a single deferral. For postgraduate taught study, applicants can make a request via their online application portal and requests for deferral will typically be accepted where there are unforeseeable life events and circumstances outside of the applicants’ control.
Reasons typically accepted for deferral include bereavement due to the loss of a close family member; serious illness and health problems; victim of a natural disaster; victim of conflict and political unrest that prohibits travel to the UK; personal accident or injury of a significant nature; child care responsibilities or caring responsibilities; relevant work experience/placements/internships; military service; change of employment circumstances; unforeseen ATAS delays; and unforeseen Visa delays.
Reasons not typically accepted for deferral include being unsuccessful in securing funding (e.g. scholarship), except in cases of the Sanctuary Scholarship, and undertaking employment or travel unrelated to the degree programme applied for.
Where a candidate with disabilities is offered a place and reasonable adjustments cannot be implemented in time for the beginning of the academic year for which the offer has been made, alternative arrangements will be discussed, and a deferral or transfer to another course may be offered where appropriate.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If you receive an offer from us, it is stated as either conditional or unconditional.
**Conditional offer**
Your offer could be conditional for a number of reasons, such as:
- you are still awaiting results, either academic or English language
- we need to verify your qualifications
- you have to meet other non-academic entry requirements such as an Occupational Health check
- you need to pay a tuition fee deposit, if applicable to your programme
The offer letter will clearly state any academic or non-academic conditions that you need to meet along with the given deadlines. We will ask you to send us evidence confirming that you have satisfied the conditions specified in your offer letter. You should upload the evidence in your applicant portal. You will also be able to see your deadlines on your applicant portal.
If your offer was initially conditional and you have met all the academic and non-academic conditions of your offer, we will send you an unconditional offer via the applicant portal. If you are an international student, you can [apply for your visa](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/studentservices/visa-and-immigration/index.page#_ga=2.46743972.2027954709.1658132442-903936629.1657527147) when you receive an unconditional offer.
